context: The deque is on the left and the vertical doubly linked list is on the right. Both run from front to rear down the page. The head is the front and the tail is the rear. Between neighboring nodes, next points down and prev points up.
description: Five frames show the initial state, adding 4 at the rear, adding 1 at the front, removing 4 from the rear, and removing 1 from the front, in that order. The new node 4 is teal and 1 is orange. The original nodes 3, 2, and 5 stay in place.

frames.announcement: The initial doubly linked list is 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5, with head 3 and tail 5.
frames.explanation: The doubly linked list starts as 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5, with head 3 and tail 5. The deque on the left is [3, 2, 5]. There is no return value.
frames.title: Initial deque

frames.announcement: Nodes 5 and 4 are linked in both directions, and the tail reference now points to 4.
frames.explanation: The call push_last(4) links a new node, 4, below 5. It sets 5.next to point to 4 and 4.prev to point to 5. The list is now 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5 ⇄ 4. The head is still 3, the tail becomes 4, and the call returns no value.
frames.title: Add 4 at the rear

frames.announcement: Nodes 1 and 3 are linked in both directions, and the head reference now points to 1.
frames.explanation: The call push_first(1) links a new node, 1, above 3. It sets 1.next to point to 3 and 3.prev to point to 1. The list is now 1 ⇄ 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5 ⇄ 4. The head becomes 1, the tail is still 4, and the call returns no value.
frames.title: Add 1 at the front

frames.announcement: Follow 4.prev to 5 and make 5 the tail. Detach node 4 and return 4.
frames.explanation: The call pop_last() follows 4.prev directly to 5, makes 5 the tail, breaks the links between 5 and 4 in both directions, and returns 4. The list is now 1 ⇄ 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5, with head 1 and tail 5.
frames.key_state: Head 1, tail 5. The deque is [1, 3, 2, 5]. The call returns 4.
frames.title: Remove 4 from the rear

frames.announcement: Follow 1.next to 3 and make 3 the head. Detach node 1 and return 1.
frames.explanation: The call pop_first() follows 1.next to 3, makes 3 the head, breaks the links between 1 and 3 in both directions, and returns 1. The list is back to 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5, with head 3 and tail 5.
frames.key_state: Head 3, tail 5. The deque is [3, 2, 5]. The call returns 1.
frames.title: Remove 1 from the front

result: With head and tail references, we can find the new rear directly when removing the old one. We simply follow prev from the tail. There is no need to traverse the list from the head. Insertion and removal at either end change only local references and take O(1) time.
summary: Head and tail references and links in both directions let us add or remove nodes at either end while the nodes in the middle stay in place.
title: Implementing a deque with a doubly linked list
